title: Distance to the previous zero
body:
For each value in column X, count the distance back to the previous zero (or to the start of the Series, whichever is closer). Store it in a new column Y. The values should be [1, 2, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 0, 1, 2].

Your updated df is checked after your code runs.
starter: # Write your code below. The value of your last line is checked.
solution:
izero = np.r_[-1, (df['X'] == 0).values.nonzero()[0]]  # positions of zeros
idx = np.arange(len(df))
df['Y'] = idx - izero[np.searchsorted(izero - 1, idx) - 1]
hint: One approach: group with (df['X'] == 0).cumsum(), number rows with cumcount(), then add 1 to the rows before the first zero.

title: Rolling mean by group
body:
Compute a rolling mean with window size 3 within each group, ignoring NaN values (a window of 3, NaN, 3 has mean 3). Return a Series in the original row order: 1.0, 1.5, 3.0, 3.0, 1.67, 3.0, 3.0, 2.0, 3.67, 2.0, 4.5, 4.0.

End with an expression; the value of your last line is checked.
setup:
df = pd.DataFrame({'group': list('aabbabbbabab'),
                   'value': [1, 2, 3, np.nan, 2, 3, np.nan, 1, 7, 3, np.nan, 8]})
starter: # Write your code below. The value of your last line is checked.
solution:
g1 = df.groupby('group')['value']
g2 = df.fillna(0).groupby('group')['value']
s = g2.rolling(3, min_periods=1).sum() / g1.rolling(3, min_periods=1).count()
s.reset_index(level=0, drop=True).sort_index()
hint: Divide a rolling sum (NaN filled with 0) by a rolling count of non-missing values, both with min_periods=1.

setup:
df = pd.DataFrame({'From_To': ['LoNDon_paris', 'MAdrid_miLAN', 'londON_StockhOlm',
                               'Budapest_PaRis', 'Brussels_londOn'],
                   'FlightNumber': [10045, np.nan, 10065, np.nan, 10085],
                   'RecentDelays': [[23, 47], [], [24, 43, 87], [13], [67, 32]],
                   'Airline': ['KLM(!)', '<Air France> (12)', '(British Airways. )',
                               '12. Air France', '"Swiss Air"']})
df['FlightNumber'] = df['FlightNumber'].interpolate().astype(int)
temp = df['From_To'].str.split('_', expand=True)
temp.columns = ['From', 'To']
temp['From'] = temp['From'].str.capitalize()

title: Expand a list column

df = pd.DataFrame({'From_To': ['LoNDon_paris', 'MAdrid_miLAN', 'londON_StockhOlm',
                               'Budapest_PaRis', 'Brussels_londOn'],
                   'FlightNumber': [10045, np.nan, 10065, np.nan, 10085],
                   'RecentDelays': [[23, 47], [], [24, 43, 87], [13], [67, 32]],
                   'Airline': ['KLM(!)', '<Air France> (12)', '(British Airways. )',
                               '12. Air France', '"Swiss Air"']})
df['FlightNumber'] = df['FlightNumber'].interpolate().astype(int)
temp = df['From_To'].str.split('_', expand=True)
temp.columns = ['From', 'To']
temp['From'] = temp['From'].str.capitalize()
temp['To'] = temp['To'].str.capitalize()
df = df.drop('From_To', axis=1).join(temp)

solution:
delays = df['RecentDelays'].apply(pd.Series)

df = df.drop('RecentDelays', axis=1).join(delays)

title: Blood pressure by age band
body:
Group patients into age bands <40, 40-59 and 60+ and return the mean sbp for each band, rounded to 1 decimal.

End with an expression; the value of your last line is checked.
setup:
rng = np.random.RandomState(42)
n = 40
patients = pd.DataFrame({
    'patient_id': range(101, 101 + n),
    'age': rng.randint(25, 80, n),
    'sex': rng.choice(['F', 'M'], n),
    'treatment': rng.choice(['A', 'B'], n),
    'bmi': rng.normal(27, 4, n).round(1),
    'sbp': rng.normal(132, 15, n).round(0),
})
patients.loc[[3, 11, 27], 'bmi'] = np.nan
patients['improved'] = (rng.rand(n) < np.where(patients['treatment'] == 'B', 0.65, 0.4)).astype(int)
starter: # Write your code below. The value of your last line is checked.
solution:
bands = pd.cut(patients['age'], bins=[0, 40, 60, 120], right=False, labels=['<40', '40-59', '60+'])
patients.groupby(bands, observed=False)['sbp'].mean().round(1)
hint: pd.cut(..., bins=[0, 40, 60, 120], right=False, labels=[...]) makes the bands.
